references.text: Isaiah prophesied that the Lord's suffering servant would be "counted among transgressors" ([ref:Jes 53:12|Isaiah 53:12]). This was directly fulfilled when Jesus was led away with two criminals to be executed.
Jesus himself quoted Isaiah 53:12 and said that "he was counted among the wicked" had to be fulfilled in him ([ref:Luk 22:37|Luke 22:37]). Luke 23:32 shows the concrete fulfillment of this word.

Mark also tells about the two thieves who were crucified with Jesus, one on his right and the other on his left side ([ref:Mark 15:27-28|Mark 15:27-28]), and explicitly links this to the prophecy that he was counted among transgressors.
Matthew likewise mentions that two thieves were crucified with Jesus, one on each side ([ref:Matt 27:38|Matthew 27:38]). This is a parallel account to Luke's presentation.
John tells that Jesus was crucified between two others, one on each side ([ref:Joh 19:18|John 19:18]). This confirms that Jesus died with criminals, as all the Gospels testify.

Luke is the only one who tells about the conversation between Jesus and the two criminals on the cross, where one repents and Jesus promises him a place in Paradise ([ref:Luk 23:39-43|Luke 23:39-43]). This is the further story of the two who were led out with Jesus in verse 32.

Peter writes that Christ suffered for us without having committed any sin ([ref:1 Pet 2:22-24|1 Peter 2:22-24]). In contrast to the two criminals who were led out with him, Jesus was completely innocent – which underscores his substitutionary suffering.
